value: humans (the source text states humans are the only animals infected)

pathogen.value: Salmonella enterica, serotypes Paratyphi A, Paratyphi B, or Paratyphi C

value: eating or drinking food or water contaminated with an infected person's feces
gradual onset of high fever over several days
rose-colored skin spots in some people
constipation more common than diarrhea in adults

mortality.value: about 10-15% without treatment, falling to under 1% with treatment

incubation_period.value: symptoms usually begin 6 to 30 days after exposure

diagnosis.value: Based on symptoms and confirmed by culturing the bacteria or detecting its DNA in blood, stool, or bone marrow; bone-marrow testing is described as the most accurate method.

treatment_overview.value: Treated with antibiotics, though resistance to several previously effective antibiotics is now common.

summary.value: Paratyphoid fever is a Salmonella infection in people that spreads through food or water contaminated by an infected person's waste, causing a prolonged fever and other flu-like symptoms. The source text describes it as a human disease with no vaccine made specifically for it, treated with antibiotics and prevented mainly through sanitation and hygiene.
